claim_assessments.interpretation: The exact claim-level relation is directly represented: a PSPAA polymer shell separates inner and outer Ag layers, an Ag bridge connects them, and the narrow polymer gap is explicitly linked to electromagnetic coupling/hotspot formation and enhanced SERS.

At the target-claim level, prior art directly establishes that gap distance controls electromagnetic hotspot strength while analyte dimensions/access determine whether those hotspots can be leveraged for SERS; independent Au/AgAu work also directly shows gap-width-dependent SERS under embedded-analyte conditions. This does not establish the narrower polymer-bridge architecture-specific controlled sweep, but that narrower statement is not the frozen target claim and must not be silently substituted here.

A close Ag-shell-coated core-satellite study directly compares dispersed-in-solution measurement with a drying-accumulated substrate and observes a large SERS intensity/reproducibility difference. It is partial, not direct, because the analyte/preparation history differs between the two measurement methods rather than measuring the same analyte-mixed preparation before and after drying.

The study establishes measurement-context-dependent SERS intensity and hotspot-number changes after drying/accumulation, but it does not establish the frozen claim's qualitative spectral-intensity-distribution or peak-profile transformation for the same Ag-shell core-satellite preparation.

primary_source_records.title: Seed-mediated synthesis and SERS performance of graphene oxide-wrapped Ag nanomushroom
verified_scope: Ag bridge connects inner and outer Ag layers through PSPAA polymer shell
polymer-separated Ag layers create plasmonic hotspots by electromagnetic coupling
SERS increases with outer Ag cap growth alongside LSPR red-shift/broadening

primary_source_records.title: Analyte Co-localization at Electromagnetic Gap Hot-Spots for Highly Sensitive (Bio)molecular Detection by Plasmon Enhanced Spectroscopies
verified_scope: systematically varied sub-10-nm plasmonic gap distances
hotspot access depends on analyte dimensions relative to gap distance
gap geometry and analyte co-localization jointly control SERS sensitivity

primary_source_records.title: Gap-Dependent Plasmon Coupling in Au/AgAu Hybrids for Improved SERS Performance
verified_scope: Au/AgAu gap width was experimentally tuned
SERS decreased as one-gap width increased from about 0.8 nm to 3.8 nm
trend attributed to adjustable plasmon coupling/electric-field enhancement

primary_source_records.title: Three-Dimensional SERS Substrates Formed with Plasmonic Core-Satellite Nanostructures
verified_scope: Ag-shell-coated plasmonic core-satellite nanostructures were measured dispersed in solution
the same nanostructure class was accumulated by drying droplets on hydrophobic PDMS
dried/accumulated substrates produced much stronger and more reproducible SERS
preparation histories were not identical because analyte was introduced after drying in the accumulated-substrate method
